title: A customer change through the Open API follows the new customer
custom_preconds:
BLOCKED ON RELEASE: this test checks the Open API story of Internal Work Orders (SV-11833), which is built after the Open API refactoring and does not ship with the core release. Do not run it now. It can be tested once SV-11833 is released.

Preconditions

  • Use an Open API key for the test organization, the Open API documentation, and a tool that sends API requests.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Approved, billable, with one approved labor line of 2.0 hours.
custom_steps:
1. Send PATCH for work order 1 through the Open API changing its customer to customer B.
  2. Open work order 1 in ShopView.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The change is accepted, with no window.

Step 2:

  • Work order 1 shows the "Internal" badge and no prices.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11833 (Story 11, Open API and webhooks)

  • S11-R4: “Writes: a work order created through the API takes the classification and the category of its customer and asset (S2-R1); No Charge cannot be set through the API in this version, on a work order or on a line; prices sent on the lines of an internal or no-charge work order are dropped and cost and hours are kept (S2-E1); a customer change through the API follows S2-R7 without the dialogs. POST /v1/invoices (disabled today, to be enabled for GA) refuses an internal or no-charge work order with the error "This work order is internal or no charge. Close it in ShopView." and accepts a billable work order with no-charge lines, invoicing them at 0.”
  • S2-R7: “Changing the customer on a work order works as today (not offered on an invoiced or paid billable work order, as today, nor on a closed internal or no-charge work order, S2-R9); until then the classification follows the new customer: to an internal customer the work order becomes internal (prices removed, costs and hours kept, no Convert actions); to a regular customer from an internal one it becomes billable (lines priced as in S2-R6). A No Charge mark and its category survive a change to another regular customer; a no-charge work order moved to an internal customer becomes internal and loses its category. The Change Customer dialog says what will happen to the prices and, when the work order stays internal or no charge, adds "Shop supplies resets to [customer]'s minimum ($[amount])." (without 'See Financial Data' the sentence omits the amount).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
